rows.note: Use 癲 for uninhibited or rowdy behaviour and for something crazy, amazing, or wildly surprising; it is the all-purpose choice for these colloquial senses.

example.english: Your party last night was wild.
example.traditional: 你哋尋晚個派對真係癲到爆。
example.jyutping: nei5 dei6 cam4 maan5 go3 paai3 deoi3 zan1 hai6 din1 dou3 baau3

rows.note: Use 野生 as the all-purpose choice for animals or plants that are undomesticated or living outside human care, including things obtained from them.

example.english: These wild berries were picked by the mountainside.
example.traditional: 呢啲野生莓係喺山邊摘返嚟㗎。
example.jyutping: ni1 di1 je5 saang1 mui4 hai6 hai2 saan1 bin1 zaak6 faan1 lei4 gaa3

rows.note: Use 亂糟糟 for wild-looking hair, clothing, or surroundings that are messy, tangled, or untidy.

example.english: Your room looks wild and messy.
example.jyutping: nei5 gaan1 fong2 gaau2 dou3 lyun6 zou1 zou1 gam2

rows.note: Use 火滾 when someone is furious or extremely angry, rather than merely behaving wildly.

example.english: I was wild with anger when I heard them accuse you like that.
example.traditional: 聽到佢咁樣屈你，我真係火滾。
example.jyutping: teng1 dou3 keoi5 gam3 joeng2 wat1 nei5 ngo5 zan1 hai6 fo2 gwan2
